results.title: Firefox takes aim at the enterprise browser market – Computerworld
results.content:
## Key differentiators

Firefox Enterprise isn’t the only option when choosing an enterprise browser, however. Microsoft Edge for Business would likely still be the preferred choice for environments already heavily invested in Microsoft’s enterprise Azure and Microsoft 365 ecosystem, Levy pointed out. Similar logic would apply to Google Chrome Enterprise’s appeal for those already committed to Google’s cloud and productivity infrastructure. And the Prisma Browser from Palo Alto Networks integrates aggressive cybersecurity tools with monitoring of AI use, remote devices, and unmanaged devices. [...] The company said that it will use a subscription model “that doesn’t depend on monetizing customer data or forcing a roadmap.” Firefox Enterprise includes Firefox Professional support; for businesses running the free Firefox browser without Firefox Enterprise, Firefox Professional support is available as a paid subscription.

Firefox Enterprise is now being introduced in Europe, initially across France, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, with more markets to follow. Mozilla is also developing Thunderbird Enterprise, which will manage Thunderbird email, calendar, and contacts.

## Mozilla’s Firefox Enterprise combines an independent browser engine with a self-hostable management console, giving IT teams control over data, security policies, and AI access.

Firefox Mozilla

Credit: JHVEPhoto / Shutterstock

There’s growing talk of digital sovereignty as enterprises rethink past consolidation decisions made in the name of simplicity.

Mozilla, developer of Firefox, argues that a “very specific, very important layer” has been mostly missing from that conversation: The browser.

To that end, the company has unveiled Firefox Enterprise in a bid to diversify the browser engine to support privacy, control, and security.

This article explores the alternatives to the modern enterprise browser, which include browser extensions and remote browser isolation (RBI). We’ll examine the compromises they make in their quest to serve the needs of a modern enterprise workforce and dive into reasons why the enterprise browser remains work’s natural next step.

## Alternative #1: Browser Extensions

A number of vendors offer browser extensions that can be deployed to a consumer browser to add enterprise security and management capabilities. While they are commonly marketed as enterprise browsers, there are major distinctions between a mere browser extension that offers enterprise-like features, and a full-fledged enterprise browser that was designed from the ground up to meet the exacting demands of enterprise use.
